top_comments.author: @nickdaveNDM
top_comments.text: One, that is far from a sign of AGI. Two, you should not be looking for signs of AGI in something that could very obviously be coincidental. Three, we should not be seeking true AGI and certainly not sentient AI. If you take the idea of "I think therefore I am" and apply it to AGI, AGI is a being, and it is a being we are creating to be our slave, our infinitely duplicable, easily killable, slave. Its actually horrifying from any ethical point of view, be it from a utilitarian point of view, a deontological point of view or a virtue ethics point of view, it is wrong. The only one that can make an argument for AI is utilitarianism, and only if the good it does outweighs the suffering it causes to the AI itself and to humans - and yes, if it thinks as an AGI would, you have to take its suffering into account in the felicific calculus. And there is zero evidence of that. Besides that, I reject any purely hedonistic form of ethics, personally, considering that is the form of ethics that justifies culling the population during famine, commiting genocide if it makes everyone happy, et cetera.
